verdict_text:
NO

The merge arithmetic takes the second task vector against the already-merged tensor rather than against the unmodified base: it computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1-base)` and then `tmp + λ(ft2-tmp)`, which equals `base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base) - λ²(ft1-base)`. That is short of the required result by `0.16*(ft1-base)` on every one of the 48 MLP tensors, violating clause 2 of "Required result" (and the explicitly warned-about ordering hazard: each task vector must be taken against the unmodified base). Since 0.16 times a real task vector is far above the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance, grading of the 48 merged tensors will fail. Everything else — key-set and shared-tensor verification, the 48/114 counts, unchanged tensors copied from base, single output file — matches the specification.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
